topics.title: US-Iran strikes lift oil prices
topics.summary: Oil prices rose and U.S. stocks slipped after renewed U.S.-Iran attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy shipments.
topics.discussionPrompt: If studio costs jumped because fuel got expensive, what budget line would everyone defend the hardest?

topics.title: House returns to funding fight
topics.summary: U.S. House lawmakers returned from recess with a stopgap spending bill at the top of the agenda as leaders try to avoid a shutdown deadline.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had to pass a last-minute budget, who would make the spreadsheet and who would keep adding snacks?

topics.title: Ukraine faces faster drone attacks
topics.summary: Russia's growing use of jet-powered drones has strained Ukrainian air defenses and disrupted daily routines around Kyiv, including food deliveries and school planning.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the characters had to redesign a routine around constant interruptions, who would adapt fastest and who would over-plan every minute?

topics.title: Advanced AI worries finance leaders
topics.summary: Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey warned G20 officials that frontier AI could create cyber and market risks if financial systems adopt it without stronger safeguards.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio let an AI handle money decisions, what rule would the characters add before trusting it?

topics.title: NHS pharmacies add cholesterol checks
topics.summary: England's NHS said about 100 high-street pharmacies will offer quick cholesterol checks this autumn to help spot heart and stroke risks earlier.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who in the studio would actually go for a quick health check, and who would need three reminders and a bribe?

topics.title: AI medical scribes face scrutiny
topics.summary: Healthwatch England warned that AI tools used to write doctors' notes can mix up drug names and diagnoses, putting more pressure on verification and correction systems.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI took notes in the studio, what funny but important detail would it probably misunderstand first?

topics.title: Heat deaths may be undercounted
topics.summary: An NPR and Boston University investigation estimated U.S. heat-related deaths are far higher than official counts, highlighting gaps in how heat risks are recorded.
topics.discussionPrompt: When it gets dangerously hot, what small practical habit would each character push on the rest of the group?

topics.title: Qantas crews back strike option
topics.summary: Qantas ground crews voted for the right to strike during a pay and safety dispute, raising the possibility of travel disruption in Australia.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a trip got delayed by a workplace dispute, who would sympathize first and who would start troubleshooting the itinerary?

topics.title: Iceland rejects EU talks
topics.summary: Icelandic voters narrowly rejected reopening European Union accession talks, keeping the country's current mix of NATO, Schengen, and single-market ties in place.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio had to vote on joining a bigger organization, what would be the dealbreaker issue for each character?

topics.title: Sagitta stands out in night sky
topics.summary: Skywatchers are being pointed toward Sagitta, a small arrow-shaped constellation that is easier to spot from darker skies during late-summer evenings.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone had to name a constellation after something in the studio, what shape would they swear they could see?
